title: Underwater explosions rupture the Nord Stream 1 and 2 gas pipelines in the Baltic Sea
body:
On 26 September 2022, underwater explosions caused gas leaks on three of the four pipes of the Nord Stream 1 and Nord Stream 2 pipelines, making them inoperable. Both Nord Stream 1 pipes were ruptured, as was Nord Stream 2 pipe A, while Nord Stream 2 pipe B was not ruptured. There were four leak sites in total, in the Danish and Swedish exclusive economic zones near the Danish island of Bornholm, in international waters.

The Geological Survey of Denmark recorded two seismic events on Bornholm, and other regional stations also recorded them. Reported magnitudes were 2.3 at 02:03 CEST on pipe NS2 A, and 2.1 at 19:03 CEST for the other leaks. The signals matched underwater explosions rather than natural earthquakes.

Sweden concluded in November 2022 that the damage was gross sabotage, based on explosive residue. Denmark and Sweden closed their investigations in February 2024 without assigning responsibility. Germany's investigation continued and in 2023 linked a yacht, the Andromeda, to the attack. A Russian proposal for an independent UN Security Council inquiry failed in March 2023. No state has been officially identified as responsible. Russia and Ukraine have each been the subject of speculation, and Ukraine denied involvement.
